answer: Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 5 bits per word is rejected before grading, because it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. Because the entropy is measured at the karst gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the garden audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. A farm emitting 137 variations of one paragraph thus forfeits for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the ledge panel. That is 35 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
